replacements.old: `createPerceptionFrame` builds its optional physical-contact grid from current maximum body radius/height rather than the 28-unit vision cell size. The query still includes conservative horizontal and vertical body extent, preserves source order and performs the unchanged exact overlap/barrier checks. No contact count, physical range or sensory authority is reduced. Frame construction still samples the world; this is not a persistent regional index or a fix for general million-player scaling.
replacements.new: `prepareExposure` in `packages/domain/src/encounter-cache.ts` owns the current physical-contact source grid, separately from the sight grid. Contact candidates use conservative current body radii/heights, preserve source order and pass exact overlap/barrier checks; there is no contact-count cap or reduced sensory authority. NP02 maintains source membership from complete warm phase changes and selects observers near old/new positions. Cold, unknown, overflowed or policy-invalidated preparation still rebuilds conservatively; affected-observer queries and broader publication costs remain. The earlier `createPerceptionFrame` implementation is removed. [NP02 evidence](../verification/perception-reaction-intake.md#np02-sensory-preparation--october-3-2026) distinguishes this current mechanism from the historical contact experiment below.

replacements.old: For accelerated-play qualification, copy a scenario outside the repository and set `execution` to `native-slice`, `speed` to `8`, and `steps` to a representative sustained duration (for example 2400). Compare it with `single-step` on the same scenario and acquisition policy. The profiler measures actual consumed simulated time and fails on non-progress; it never assumes every invocation advances the requested duration. A native-slice result still excludes server scheduling, persistence and rendering.
replacements.new: For native elapsed-time comparisons, copy a scenario outside the repository and set an actual `durationSeconds` span (for example 2400), explicit `warmupSeconds`, `intervalSeconds` and `maxIntervals`; set `speed` to `8` only for the headroom calculation. Compare matched inputs and actual progressed time, with a one-second offered interval as a diagnostic reference where useful. The current strict parser has no `execution` field or `single-step`/`native-slice` modes. Bound the run with `timeoutSeconds`, report blocked/non-progress results, and do not assume every call advances its offered duration. This remains native CPU isolation, not accelerated-play qualification through server scheduling, persistence or rendering.
